auraWeb.name: Aura Web
auraWeb.description: I fully developed the frontend for a decentralized exchange (DEX) on the TON blockchain from scratch. The project is built on React and Redux Toolkit, ensuring reliable application state management and data predictability. WebSockets are integrated for real-time market quotes, and interaction with the server occurs through REST API. The key feature of the interface is integration with Tonconnect, allowing users to connect their TON wallets directly through the application. After connection, all main operations become available: depositing funds to the platform, investing in liquidity pools, and instant withdrawal of funds. WebSockets provide real-time display of current market changes without page reload. The frontend architecture is designed with future scalability in mind. Currently, integration with EVM-compatible networks (Ethereum, BSC, and others) is in development, which will expand the platform's functionality and reach a wider audience in the future.

auraTma.name: Aura TMA
auraTma.description: A Telegram Mini Application that combines gamification elements with trading learning mechanics. The project is built on React and Redux Toolkit, with backend interaction through REST API and WebSockets. Through Tonconnect, users connect their TON wallets and get access to all application functions directly inside Telegram. The main feature of the platform is learning trading basics in a game format. Users complete tasks (subscribing to Telegram channels, viewing content, and other activities) and receive tokens for them. There's also a mini-game where you need to 'catch' falling tokens, making the accumulation process more engaging. The interface displays token balance both on the exchange and in the connected wallet. A referral system works for user engagement: you can invite friends and receive bonuses. Accumulated tokens are available for withdrawal to the wallet or exchange through the built-in swap. The project shows how to effectively combine learning, game mechanics, and real financial operations in a Telegram mini-application format.

artisan.name: Artisan Kiln
artisan.description: I developed the frontend for an interactive ecommerce application called The Artisan Kiln using Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Redux Toolkit. The application includes a shopping cart with dynamic calculations, an interactive 6x6 drag & drop design tool, a checkout form with validation powered by React Hook Form and Zod, and support for multiple payment methods. Additionally, I implemented a responsive layout, touch drag & drop support for mobile devices, animations with Framer Motion, and unit/integration testing using Vitest and React Testing Library.

statusRk.name: Status RK
statusRk.description: A turnkey corporate website — from design (in collaboration with a designer) to final deployment on the domain. The project was developed in close collaboration with a designer: we jointly worked out page structures, visual solutions, and user scenarios, after which I fully implemented the frontend in React with responsive layout for all device types. The website features a feedback form with email sending to the domain mailbox — handled by a lightweight PHP backend that I also wrote and integrated into the project. Users can fill in contact details, send a message, and it is guaranteed to be delivered to the company's mailbox without using third-party services. After development completion, I deployed the site to the domain, configured hosting, and ensured correct operation of all components in production. As a result, the client received a fully ready-to-use corporate website with clean code, a modern interface, and stable feedback functionality.

sw.name: Simple Wealth
sw.description: Simple Wealth is a multi-page, responsive, and cross-browser website built with pure HTML and powered by the Gulp task runner. The project includes several pages with a well-structured layout and semantic markup. The website is fully responsive, ensuring proper display across different devices — from mobile phones to desktops — and has been tested in popular browsers. Gulp is used to automate the development workflow, including file minification, image optimization, preprocessor handling, and efficient project structure management for a smooth and productive development process.

alphaBeat.name: AlphaBeat
alphaBeat.description: AlphaBeat is a mini-game built with React and MockAPI that helps train alphabet knowledge in the correct sequence and speed. The player needs to mark all letters in order as quickly as possible. Upon completion, the result — completion time — is displayed. It can be saved to the database and then viewed in the overall results list. There's also an option to restart the game for another attempt and improve your record.

dashka.name: Dashboard
dashka.description: Dashboard is an analytical web application built on React using Chart.js for data visualization. The project displays key metrics in the form of interactive graphs and charts (line, bar, pie), allowing you to clearly track the dynamics of indicators. Data can be updated in real time or loaded from an API. Dashboard helps you quickly analyze statistics, compare indicators, and make decisions based on visually presented information.

uiwave.name: UIWave
uiwave.description: UIWave is a UI experimentation and A/B testing service. It helps you create experiments for UIs and test them on your users. Instead of changing your UI and hoping for the best, you can use UIWave to test your changes and see how they affect your users first. You can do that by allocating a percentage of your users to the experiment and then comparing the results of the experiment to the results of the control group.

about.title: About me
about.text:
Hi, I'm Adil, a front-end developer with 5 years of experience.
I develop and maintain projects on React / Next.js, covering the entire client side of web applications.

During this time, I have worked in startups, established companies, and as a freelancer, so I have a good understanding of different processes, requirements, and development speeds.
In projects, I took on the responsibility of front-end team lead: I participated in architectural decisions, code reviews, and team organization.

Layout, complex logic, working with APIs, optimization, and UX — I feel confident at every level of front-end development and know how to bring interfaces to production quality.

I will be happy to answer your questions and am open to further cooperation!
